arxiv-2205-12159.title: Do it Like the Doctor: How We Can Design a Model That Uses Domain Knowledge to Diagnose Pneumothorax
arxiv-2205-12159.creator: Glen Smith, Qiao Zhang, Christopher J. MacLellan
arxiv-2205-12159.description: Abstract Computer-aided diagnosis for medical imaging is a well-studied field that aims to provide real-time decision support systems for physicians. These systems attempt to detect and diagnose a plethora of medical conditions across a variety of image diagnostic technologies including ultrasound, x-ray, MRI, and CT.

arxiv-2304-12054.title: Differential equations for Gaussian statistical models with rational maximum likelihood estimator
arxiv-2304-12054.creator: Carlos Améndola, Lukas Gustafsson, Kathlén Kohn, Orlando Marigliano, Anna Seigal
arxiv-2304-12054.description: Abstract . We study multivariate Gaussian statistical models whose maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) is a rational function of the observed data. We establish a one-to-one correspondence between such models and the solutions to a nonlinear first-order partial differential equation (PDE).

arxiv-2310-06728.title: Fuzzy semigroups via semigroups
arxiv-2310-06728.creator: Anjeza Krakulli
arxiv-2310-06728.description: Abstract The theory of fuzzy semigroups is a branch of mathematics that arose in early 90’s as an effort to characterize properties of semigroups by the properties of their fuzzy subsystems which include, fuzzy subsemigroups and their alike, fuzzy one (resp. two) sided ideals, fuzzy quasi-ideals, fuzzy bi-ideals etc.

arxiv-2401-01881.title: Robust Control Barrier Functions using Uncertainty Estimation with Application to Mobile Robots
arxiv-2401-01881.creator: Ersin Daş, Joel W. Burdick
arxiv-2401-01881.description: Abstract This paper proposes a safety-critical control design approach for nonlinear control affine systems in the presence of matched and unmatched uncertainties. Our constructive framework couples control barrier function (CBF) theory with a new uncertainty estimator to ensure robust safety.

arxiv-2401-17222.title: Stress and Alignment Response to Curved Obstacles in Growing Bacterial Monolayers
arxiv-2401-17222.creator: Blake Langeslay 1, Will Fahy 2, Gabriel Juarez 2
arxiv-2401-17222.description: Abstract Monolayers of growing bacteria, confined within channel geometries, exhibit self-organization into a highly aligned laminar state along the axis of the channel. Although this phenomenon has been observed in experiments and simulations under various boundary conditions, the underlying physical mechanism driving this alignment remains unclear.

arxiv-2402-07844.title: Mercury: A Code Efficiency Benchmark for Code Large Language Models
arxiv-2402-07844.creator: Mingzhe Du, Anh Tuan Luu, Bin Ji, Qian Liu, See-Kiong Ng
arxiv-2402-07844.description: Abstract Amidst the recent strides in evaluating Large Language Models for Code (Code LLMs), existing benchmarks have mainly focused on the functional correctness of generated code, neglecting the importance of their computational efficiency. To fill the gap, we present Mercury , the first code efficiency benchmark for Code LLMs.

arxiv-2407-14597.title: Antenna subtraction for final-state radiation at N 3 LO
arxiv-2407-14597.description: Abstract I review some aspects of antenna subtraction at next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in QCD and provide motivation for its extension to N 3 LO. Next, I introduce the antenna functions required for the construction of infrared counterterms for final-state radiation at this order.

arxiv-2506-20271.title: Broadband Dielectric Analysis of Clays: Impact of Cation Exchange Capacity, Water Content, and Porosity Journal: arXiv Preprint
arxiv-2506-20271.creator: Felix Schmidt, Norman Wagner, Ines Mulder, Katja Emmerich, Thierry Bore, and Jan Bumberger
arxiv-2506-20271.description: Abstract Clay-rich soils and sediments are key components of near-surface systems, influencing water retention, ion exchange, and structural stability. Their complex dielectric behavior under moist conditions arises from electrostatic interactions between charged mineral surfaces and exchangeable cations, forming diffuse double layers that govern transport and retention processes.

arxiv-2507-13988.title: A Ghost Lemma for Commutative Ring Homomorphisms via André-Quillen Homology Thanks: The author was partly supported by the National Science Foundation under grant No. 2001368 and No. 1840190.
arxiv-2507-13988.creator: Daniel McCormick
arxiv-2507-13988.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniel McCormick. We adapt the theory of ghost maps from derived categories to the setting of commutative rings using André-Quillen homology. The Frobenius endomorphism is a primary example of a ghost map in this setting. We prove an analogue of the ghost lemma for rings and demonstrate its utility by deducing a characteristic independent generalization of Kunz’s theorem and an analogue for complete intersection rings. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 13D03 (primary); 13D05, 13D09, 13H05, 13H10 1.

arxiv-2509-01350.title: Error Notebook-Guided, Training-Free Part Retrieval in 3D CAD Assemblies via Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2509-01350.creator: Yunqing Liu, Nan Zhang & Zhiming Tan
arxiv-2509-01350.description: Abstract Effective specification-aware part retrieval within complex CAD assemblies is essential for automated design verification and downstream engineering tasks. However, directly using LLMs/VLMs to this task presents some challenges: the input sequences may exceed model token limits, and even after processing, performance remains unsatisfactory. Moreover, fine-tuning LLMs/VLMs requires significant computational resources, and for many high-performing general-use proprietary models (e.g.

arxiv-2510-04412.title: Monomial curves and locally linear resolution
arxiv-2510-04412.creator: Takayuki Hibi and Peter Schenzel
arxiv-2510-04412.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Takayuki Hibi and Peter Schenzel. For four elements of a Noetherian ring we construct complexes of free modules of length three (resp. five) by an explicit description of the homomorphisms of the free modules. We provide exactness criteria for them. As an application we use these results in order to describe explicit the minimal free resolution of the Hartshorne–Rao module of a monomial curve lying on a smooth quadric. Also it provides an example of linearly generated module with syzygies of arbitrary high degree.

arxiv-2510-05680.title: A Bivariate DAR( 1 1 ) model for ordinal time series
arxiv-2510-05680.creator: Anna Nalpantidi and Dimitris Karlis
arxiv-2510-05680.description: Abstract We present a bivariate vector valued discrete autoregressive model of order 1 1 (BDAR( 1 1 )) for discrete time series. The BDAR( 1 1 ) model assumes that each time series follows its own univariate DAR( 1 1 ) model with dependent random mechanisms that determine from which component the current status occurs and dependent innovations.

arxiv-2601-20240.title: Understanding npm Developers’ Practices, Challenges, and Recommendations for Secure Package Development Conference: 19th International Conference International Workshop on Cooperative and Human Aspects of Software ; April 12–18, 2026; Rio de Janeiro, Brazil 19th International Conference Internationa
arxiv-2601-20240.creator: Anthony Peruma, Truman Choy, Gerald Lee, Italo De Oliveira Santos
arxiv-2601-20240.description: Abstract . Background: The Node Package Manager (npm) ecosystem plays a vital role in modern software development by providing a vast repository of packages and tools that developers can use to implement their software systems. However, recent vulnerabilities in third-party packages have led to serious security breaches, compromising the integrity of applications that depend on them.

arxiv-2602-07150.title: On Randomness in Agentic Evals
arxiv-2602-07150.creator: Bjarni Haukur Bjarnason, André Silva, Martin Monperrus
arxiv-2602-07150.description: Abstract Agentic systems are evaluated on benchmarks where agents interact with environments to solve tasks. Most papers report a pass@1 score computed from a single run per task, assuming this gives a reliable performance estimate. We test this assumption by collecting 60,000 agentic trajectories on SWE-Bench-Verified , spanning three models and two scaffolds.

arxiv-2602-22818.title: LeRobot: An Open-Source Library for End-to-End Robot Learning
arxiv-2602-22818.creator: Remi Cadene * Hugging Face &Simon Aliberts * Hugging Face &Francesco Capuano * † University of Oxford &Michel Aractingi * Hugging Face &Adil Zouitine * Hugging Face &Pepijn Kooijmans * Hugging Face &Jade Choghari * Hugging Face &Martino Russi * Hugging Face &Caroline Pascal * Hugging Face &Steven Pa
arxiv-2602-22818.description: Abstract Robotics is undergoing a significant transformation powered by advances in high-level control techniques based on machine learning, giving rise to the field of robot learning. Recent progress in robot learning has been accelerated by the increasing availability of affordable teleoperation systems, large-scale openly available datasets, and scalable learning-based methods.

plos-pone-0004582.description: PLOS ONE research article. Autism is a complex childhood neurodevelopmental disorder with a strong genetic basis. pmc-10542617.title: Predicting Blomia tropicalis allergens using a multiomics approach
pmc-10542617.creator: Jan Hubert, Susanne Vrtala, Bruno Sopko, Scot E. Dowd, Qixin He, Pavel B. Klimov, Karel Harant, Pavel Talacko, Tomas Erban
pmc-10542617.description: BackgroundThe domestic mite Blomia tropicalis is a major source of allergens in tropical and subtropical regions. Despite its great medical importance, the allergome of this mite has not been sufficiently studied. Only 14 allergen groups have been identified in B.

pmc-11527820.title: Haptoglobin phenotype and levels in type 2 diabetes and effects of fenofibrate
pmc-11527820.creator: Andrzej S Januszewski, Hayden K Young, Kwok‐Leung Ong, Liping Li, Rachel L O’Connell, Timothy J Lyons, Clare Kelly, Dessi P Zaharieva, David R Sullivan, Russell S Scott, Anthony C Keech, Alicia J Jenkins, the FIELD Study Investigators
pmc-11527820.description: Aims/HypothesisIn diabetes haptoglobin (Hp) 2 vs Hp 1 allelic product is associated with cardiac and renal complications. Few studies report both Hp phenotype and Hp levels. In a Fenofibrate Intervention and Event Lowering in Diabetes (FIELD) trial substudy we evaluated the Hp phenotype, Hp levels, and fenofibrate effects.

pmc-11641476.title: New Insights into Kidney Diseases
pmc-11641476.creator: Kan Katayama, Kaoru Dohi
pmc-11641476.description: factors. In addition to existing drugs with proven nephroprotective effects, such as renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system inhibitors [3,4,5] and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors [6,7,8], new drugs are also under development. pmc-11645793.title: O051 Understanding the uptake of non-invasive ventilation in motor neurone disease: results of a national survey
pmc-11645793.creator: M Graco, K Carey, K Russo, N Sheers, D Berlowitz
pmc-11645793.description: IntroductionNon-invasive ventilation (NIV) is an effective therapy for extending survival and enhancing quality of life in people with motor neurone disease (pwMND). According to Australian registry data from 2005-2015, just 19% of pwMND ever commenced NIV. This study aimed to estimate the current rates of NIV uptake among pwMND and identify demographic factors associated with its uptake.MethodsNational cross-sectional survey.

pmc-11691828.title: CLINICIAN AWARENESS, ATTITUDES, AND INTEREST IN BLOOD TESTS FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE
pmc-11691828.creator: Karen Tracy, Julie Wood, Ben Tiede, Emily Scholler
pmc-11691828.description: Clinical research demonstrates the value of early detection of dementia, including dementia caused by Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and related disorders. Yet, timely and accurate diagnosis of AD in clinical practice remains challenging. The most widely used biomarkers to aid diagnosis of AD are positron emission tomography (PET) scans and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers.

pmc-11714491.title: Usage Patterns of Anticoagulant Therapy in Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment or Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11714491.creator: Haixin Zhang, Quanwu Zhang, Amir Abbas Tahami Monfared, Michael C Irizarry
pmc-11714491.description: BackgroundThis study aims to describe usage patterns and risk factors associated with anticoagulant therapy in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or Alzheimer’s disease (AD).MethodsThe United States Medicare claims database (2008– 18) was used to identify patients aged ≥65 years with MCI or AD and to evaluate their anticoagulant use from 2016– 17.

pmc-12522154.title: α-Ketoglutaric acid in Ugi reactions and Ugi/aza-Wittig tandem reactions
pmc-12522154.creator: Vladyslav O Honcharov, Yana I Sakhno, Olena H Shvets, Vyacheslav E Saraev, Svitlana V Shishkina, Tetyana V Shcherbakova, Valentyn A Chebanov, Marine Desage-El Murr
pmc-12522154.description: A small library of bis- and tetraamides was synthesized by the Ugi reaction with α-ketoglutaric acid, tert-butyl isocyanide, aromatic aldehydes, and aromatic amines. When o-azidoanilines were used, azidated peptidomimetics were obtained, the post-cyclization of which by the aza-Wittig reaction yielded a series of substituted 3-(3-oxo-3,4-dihydroquinoxalin-2-yl)propanoic acids containing a pharmacophore quinoxalinone moiety.

pmc-12769751.title: Measuring the magnetic fields in the chromospheres of low-mass stars
pmc-12769751.creator: Tianqi Cang, Pascal Petit, Jean-François Donati, Hui Tian, Jianning Fu, Hao Li, Stefano Bellotti, Xueying Hu, Xiaoyu Ma, Arturo Lopez Ariste, Keyu Xing, Julien Morin, Hongpeng Lu, Weikai Zong
pmc-12769751.description: Magnetic fields in the upper atmospheres of solar-like stars are believed to provide an enormous amount of energy to power the hot coronae and drive large-scale eruptions that could impact the habitability of planetary systems around these stars. However, these magnetic fields have never been routinely measured on stars beyond the solar system.

pmc-13188292.title: Analysis of visual quality after implantation of diffractive multifocal intraocular lens Diff - aA in cataract patients
pmc-13188292.creator: Zhang Jingwen, Sun Louxun, Yang Yifan, Du Shanshan, Shao Jingzhi, Zhang Fengyan
pmc-13188292.description: ObjectiveTo explore the visual quality analysis of cataract patients after implantation of the aspheric diffractive multifocal intraocular lens (IOL) Diff-aA IOL.MethodsThis was a prospective cohort study. From September 2024 to September 2025, 93 cataract patients (93 eyes) from the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University were recruited.

pmc-13240424.title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Single‐Cell Analyses Identify ATP1A1 as a Prognostic and Immune‐Associated Factor in Esophageal Cancer
pmc-13240424.creator: Huishen Yan, Liang He
pmc-13240424.description: BackgroundEsophageal cancer is a highly aggressive malignancy with poor prognosis and limited molecular markers for effective risk stratification and therapeutic guidance. Mitochondrial stress–related pathways are increasingly recognized as important regulators of tumor progression and immune modulation; however, their clinical relevance in esophageal cancer remains insufficiently characterized.MethodsTranscriptomic and clinical data of esophageal cancer were obtained from public databases.

pmc-13257235.title: Identification of Dermatological Conditions Manageable in Primary Care: A Multidisciplinary Consensus Analysis
pmc-13257235.creator: Bekir Aktura, Esmehan Ayşit, Feyza Bayram Çatak, Ece Uysal Kasap, Pınar Kıran, Beyza Arpacı Saylar, Zafer Türkoğlu, Defne Özkoca, Nazlı Caf, Mehmet Onur Gökalp, Hediye Eker, Mehmet Burhan Küçükoğlu
pmc-13257235.description: Highlights Across a multidisciplinary commission assessment, 51.5% of tertiary dermatology outpatient visits were judged manageable in primary care—27.5% by a family physician directly and a further 24.0% with teledermatology support.Specialist self-referral was very common: 82.2% of patients reached the tertiary dermatology clinic without any prior family-physician visit, consistent with a health system that does not require primary-care gatekeeping.

pmc-13270885.title: Comparison of Different Methods of Labor Induction and Their Maternal and Neonatal Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13270885.creator: Okelue E Okobi, Akinyele Oladimeji, Idayat A Durojaiye, Omowunmi Adewara, Adaora W Mochu, Oluwaferanmi Shofu, Adewale M Adedoyin, Sunday O Arifayan
pmc-13270885.description: Labor induction is a commonly used intervention in obstetric care, yet uncertainty persists regarding the comparative effectiveness and safety of mechanical, pharmacological, and combined methods across different clinical settings. Variability in practice and patient characteristics continues to influence outcomes, and clear comparative evidence remains limited.

pmc-13314916.title: Head-to-head comparison of neurodegeneration biomarkers across two analytical platforms in Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13314916.creator: Carolin Kurz, Daniela Hattenkofer, Maximilian Pihale-Haug, Anna Hufnagel, Selim Üstün Gürsel, Matthias Brendel, Boris-Stephan Rauchmann, Johannes Levin, Günter Höglinger, Robert Perneczky

pmc-13363190.title: Risk factors and prediction model for early pregnancy loss in polycystic ovary syndrome – development and validation: A retrospective and observational study
pmc-13363190.creator: Jingqi Wu, Huifang Chen, Jie Zhang, Yongquan Chen
pmc-13363190.description: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder affecting reproductive-aged women and is associated with an increased risk of early pregnancy loss (EPL). The underlying mechanisms remain multifactorial and poorly understood. This study aimed to identify key risk factors for EPL in PCOS patients and develop a corresponding predictive model.

pmc-13559135.title: Gut microbiota alterations in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit extremely preterm infants: a Chinese tertiary center study
pmc-13559135.creator: Weijuan Han, Peipei Fu, Hong Cui
pmc-13559135.description: BackgroundEarly‑life gut microbiota shapes neonatal health. Extremely preterm infants frequently experience gut dysbiosis, while relevant Chinese longitudinal data remain scarce. This study aimed to explore early gut microbiota dynamics and identify potential microbial markers in Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) extremely preterm infants.
